Unconventional: No

Comments: On August 8, 2024, inspection conducted at the former location of the Corbett 1 well site in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. Plugging was completed on November 8, 2022. This inspection follows up to IR 3754643, where during the time of that inspection it appeared that no restoration work had been done since violations were issued for Failure to Restore post-plugging under IR 3650192. No responses of any kind to violations issued under IR 3650192 have been received by the Department from the operator as of the time of this inspection.The following was observed:The former well site location appears to have been recently cleared. The access road remains unrestored. The previously observed debris that appeared to be from plugging and/or production is no longer onsite. No restoration plans or E and S BMP's were found onsite. The previously observed electrical meter associated with the well site remains on the landowner's property. However, the Department was informed by the former landowner that it was disconnected by Penelec.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that earth disturbances have occurred onsite since the time of IR 3754643, and the site remains unrestored with equipment for production remaining onsite. The Department recommends that the operator implement temporary stabilization on areas exhibiting less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage. The Department requests that a written NOV response be submitted by COB 8/28/2024 that includes clarification as to who is responsible for the recent clearing onsite.Violations continued under IR 3754643 shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8163716
Permit API: 015-23844
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: West Burlington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/27/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL289 C" Marcellus well site.Danielle Schaad (Chesapeake) called the DEP on October 26, 2023 to report an estimated 13 gallon release of production liquid from a vac truck hose onto the pad surface occurred at about 1400 hrs that day.MR Dirt removed the pad material impacted by the production liquid. I spoke Dakota Manning (Creston Environmental) site. They confirmed the cleanup with electrical conductivity (<1.0 mS/cm) readings of pad material slurry. I got a 0.09 mS/cm reading from the excavated area with a Hanna Soil Test probe. Violations cited to the 015-23844 permit are considered immediately corrected. MR Dirt installed Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls (5 infiltration berms) last week. Vegetation, and rock stabilize soil most of the site. There is some exposed soil where MR Dirt constructed new PCSM controls. MRDirt plans to seed/mulch soil of the new berms next week. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is in place below the new berms.Falcon Flowback Services started flowing back the 3 Marcellus wells on Monday October 16, 2023. There are 2 sandtraps and 2 heaters attched to the flow lines for each of the 3 Marcellus wells. Mularz expects Flowback will move off site in about 3 weeks.Chesapeake spudded surface holes on April 13, 2023 for 3 new Marcellus wells at this site. They finished drilling the 3 wells into the Marcellus in June 2023. Records show there is also 1 well spudded here in May 2012 and plugged in March 2013. Universal hydraulically fractured the 3 Marcellus wells on July 10-24, 2023. Deep Well Services then used a workover rig with rig assist snubbing unit to drill out plugs in the 3 wells August 1-5, 2023. Environmental Oilfield Solutions regraded the gravel pad surface during a previous inspection on August 16, 2023. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.33-0.90mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 75FJLP

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/29/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8250187
Permit API: 123-49050
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/29/2025
Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. I arrived onsite and found a hose running down hill from a tank battery on Farm Lane that was used to hold presumed fresh water during the recent completion of this well. The well operator was draining the water tank and using it to water their freshly seeded and mulched areas. I used my conductivity probe and determined the water being discharged from the tank was not suitable to be dispersed to the ground as the conductance of the fluid was in excess of 16000S, which is above the allowable limit of 1000S. The operator immediately shut the valve and ceased the discharge. It is estimated over 1 barrel of fluid was released prior to closing the valve. Mr. Branch called to get additional equipment onsite to begin remediating the release. It was advised to get a vac truck for any standing water, and the mini excavator on site to begin soil removal.From the end of the discharge hose, the water ran approximately 35 feet in a westerly direction across a portion of the site, reaching an open earthen drainage ditch, this ditch connects to the local storm sewer somewhere along Crestview Blvd. Flowing water in the storm sewer was observed at the bottom of Crestview Blvd, due to lack of access I was unable to get my conductivity probe into the water to determine if it was from the Brown #1 site.

Under the liner, the EC of the fluid was 1600 uS/cm.The Department recommends continuing to collect and dispose of the fluid in the northwest stormwater channel and in the sump. I made this recommendation to the company man before leaving the location. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/07/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 977710
Permit API: 083-47206
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/07/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted upon being notified by Bull Run Resources that a crude oil release had occurred from a gathering line located at this well site.Upon my arrival on the well site, Eric Clancy of Bull Run explained that a pinhole formed in a steel gathering line located behind the location (east-northeast of the well, GPS coordinate 41.80141N 78.85587W). It appears that crude oil has been discharging from this pinhole at a minimal rate for an unknown period of time.Bull Run has repaired the failure in the gathering line, which has stopped the discharge. Oil soaked soil that was excavated to locate and repair the line remains staged on the well site. Crude oil traveled alongside the southeastern corner of the location for approximately 30 feet before reaching a roadside ditch that runs along the southern edge of the spur road. Evidence of crude oil was observed across an approximate 125 foot stretch of this ditch. Field screening with a PID meter did not detect appreciable VOC readings downslope of 41.80182N 78.85616W. Oil soaked leaves and a thin layer of oil soaked soil have been excavated from the southeastern perimeter of the well site and the ditch, this material is staged on the side of the road.Bull Run has constructed an underflow dam near the southern corner of the well site and has placed numerous absorbent pads on pockets of free crude that remain in the excavated area where the line was unearthed and in the ditch. I suggested to Eric that an additional underflow dam be constructed in the ditch downslope of the point where crude has thus far migrated as a preventive measure. Additional underflow dams and/or absorbent pads/booms should also be considered elsewhere across the impacted area to improve the initial containment efforts. Finally, Eric and I discussed the potential excavation of additional soil in the immediate vicinity of the gathering line, given the presence of visible product in this area. All methods of containment should be regularly monitored and maintained.At the time of this inspection, it is estimated that approximately 10 tons of oil soaked soil and leaf litter have been excavated and are in need of disposal. Additional soil excavation will likely be conducted throughout upcoming remediation activities. At this time, the evidence available suggests that less than one barrel of crude oil was released and no watercourses were impacted by this release.It is requested that Bull Run provide a remediation plan and keep the Department apprised of any developments that pertain to the cleanup of the remaining residual crude oil associated with this release. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and determine if additional measures are required.This well is a conventional well, equipped for production with a pump jack. A site ID sign is posted on the jack. The coordinates for this well were updated as part of this inspection.

Comments: On 10/23/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of three water samples that were collected during fracking operations from three different locations at the site. During inspections #3846615 and #3846665, conducted on 10/2/2024 and 10/3/2024; the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. Samples were collected on 10/3/2024. On 10/19/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-142 was collected from the south of two puddles of water near the outfall at the center of the north perimeter berm; both puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductivity on the Altair PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. The south puddle measured 6' x 1.5' x 3 inches and the north puddle measured 10' x 3' x 2". The 16" freshwater pipeline and the 16" frac water pipeline traveled through these puddles. There was a multi-colored crusty sheen and the water left a brown film on the sample bottles. The results are shown in pictures 1-3.Sample 9551-143 was collected from within MRC basin 1 in a water/muddy area where the outfall from the center of the north perimeter berm flows into the basin. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 4-6. Sample 9551-144 was collected from within MRC basin 1, next to the east basin overflow. Water in this area field tested at 1.595 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 7-8.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, manganese, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2). This incident does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b). Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the elevated conductance, aluminum, iron, manganese, strontium and chlorides in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Violation ID: 8205475
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/23/2024
Comments: On 10/23/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of three water samples that were collected during fracking operations from three different locations at the site. During inspections #3846615 and #3846665, conducted on 10/2/2024 and 10/3/2024; the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. Samples were collected on 10/3/2024. On 10/19/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-142 was collected from the south of two puddles of water near the outfall at the center of the north perimeter berm; both puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductivity on the Altair PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. The south puddle measured 6' x 1.5' x 3 inches and the north puddle measured 10' x 3' x 2". The 16" freshwater pipeline and the 16" frac water pipeline traveled through these puddles. There was a multi-colored crusty sheen and the water left a brown film on the sample bottles. The results are shown in pictures 1-3.Sample 9551-143 was collected from within MRC basin 1 in a water/muddy area where the outfall from the center of the north perimeter berm flows into the basin. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 4-6. Sample 9551-144 was collected from within MRC basin 1, next to the east basin overflow. Water in this area field tested at 1.595 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 7-8.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, manganese, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2). This incident does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b). Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the elevated conductance, aluminum, iron, manganese, strontium and chlorides in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection at the Jobes 1 well plugging site in Georges Township, Fayette County. Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart (Next Level Energy) was on site conducting plugging operations during this inspection.The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance. However, the RCE is partially laden with sediment at the time of inspection. Additional sediment was observed in the neighboring residential yard and on Jobes Drive. The sediment observed on Jobes Drive appeared to be tracked approximately 150 feet from the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE). Significant tire rutting was observed in the neighboring residential yard and in the access road. The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is available on site.Upon arriving to the well plugging site, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart. Lockhart cautioned the Department that high-pressure lines are active around the gas well, and suggested against approaching the plugging rig during this inspection. Therefore, the area surrounding the well plugging rig was not evaluated during this inspection due to the hazards present.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE), the tire rutting in the access road, the sediment tracked onto Jobes Drive, and for conducting plugging operations in a manner that causes a public nuisance.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/09/2021 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Greene Twp, Greene county. 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 920537
Permit API: 059-24935
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2021
Comments: Prior to inspection: On 6/2/21 Range Resource's Derek Zofchak reported a produced water spill estimated at 15 gallons resulting from a pump operator "overfilling a tub" during site activities. The spill did not reportedly impact or threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth but extended roughly 60' off the site and down a fill slope. On 6/9/21 an incident inspection of the Indian Point Unit 1 Well Pad was conducted in response to an operator reported spill (CTS ID: 357202). The following was observed: >>Communication with the operator in conjunction with the inspection indicated that the spill had been fully remediated and a roll off box of impacted material was taken for disposal. >>Work crews were on site at the time of inspection adding compost filter sock (CFS) and conducting site maintenance. (Photo #1) >>An erosion channel was noted leading to the well pad near the juncture of the site access road and the pad. Remediation and stabilization are recommended. (Photo #2) >>The site was reportedly being prepared for upgrades with numerous liners, tanks and other equipment, and earth work noted. The site is less than five acres and does not appear to ever have/need an ESCGP. (Photo #3) >>Background conductivity readings as measured in several areas less than ten feet off pad were between 0.15-0.20mS. (Photo #4) >>In general conductivity readings around the pad area where between 0.4-0.8mS which may be related to pad materials (limestone) or residual impact. (Photo #5) >>The remediated spill area appeared to be as described by the operator with conductivity readings at background levels. (Photo #6) >>An area of saturated soil roughly 10'x5' near the pad liner/containment and directly adjacent to the remediated primary spill area was also significantly impacted with conductivity readings of 8.5-9.2mS. This may indicate additional spilled production fluids having leaked under the pad liner and panels. Follow up inspection needed once liner and pads are moved. The findings, a request for notification when the expanded spill area is accessible, and the need for follow up inspections were immediately communicated to Range Resources' Dennis Furmanek and Derek Zofchak. (Photo #7-8) >>Determination: The initially reported spill and the identified area of residual impact constitute violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.57(a), and 35 P.S. § 6018.301 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On June 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad.All areas that had been excavated off of the well pad due to the spill have been back filled and regraded. Violation ID: 851520

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-04
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 6/4/2019 @0930 hours. The weather was 62 degrees and sunny. Jennifer Compton, Rockdale/Tilden Marcellus, and Korey Starkey, DEP Env Trainee, was present onsite for the inspection. On 6/3/2019 at 23:20,a nitrogen pop-off unit failed allowing stimulation fluid to spray out onto containment and the grassy area surrounding the pad. Tilden deployed vac trucks to collect and return the fluid to the onsite tanks. As of today's inspection, fluid with a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm was observed pooling on the eastern and southeastern edges of the pad. A skid steer was being used to scrape up vegetation and soils, on the eastern fill slope, with an elevated field measured conductivity. Damp areas with soil exhibiting a field measured conductivity of >4.0mS/cm were observed off the southeastern corner of the pad and underneath the rig mats in the sand storage area. There is no containment under the sand storage area. A representative from Tilden's environmental contractor, C.E.C., arrived onsite and began delineating the extent of the impacted soils. Approximately 2 acres of vegetation appeared to have salt crystallization, from evaporating stimulation fluid, deposited on it. This impacted vegetation was observed to tree line east southeast of the well pad. Tilden Marcellus's spill response plan involved brush-hogging and weed whacking all impacted vegetation. This vegetation would be bagged and disposed of in an appropriate container. Impacted pad material and soils would also be removed and placed in onsite waste containers. A lined trench and sumps would be installed, in the east and southeast fill slopes, to intercept any stormwater runoff that commingled with a regulated substance from the site (thereby becoming a regulated substance). Fluid with a field measured conductivity of 13.64mS/cm was observed pooling, outside of containment, along the interior edge of the sand storage area. Sample 4427-187 was collected from this fluid. Fluid with a field measured conductivity was observed in numerous areas inside the secondary containment. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a56(a) We departed the site at 1230 hours.

From the separator, the oil line is buried and travels down gradient to the production tanks. The brine line runs on the surface down gradient. The fittings on the brine line from the separator are showing signs of corrosion and are occasionally dripping onto the ground. It appears there has been a previous discharge in the area by the appearance of the dead vegetation. The brine line was followed down gradient and observed discharging at 41.421803 N, -79.768843 W. A sample was collected (0641-119). The flow rate during sampling was much slower then observed on 03/22/19. After the sample was collected it was observed that no wells were currently pumping. The operator was called (Harry Rhodes) and notified of the violation. The Department will meet with the operator on 04/02/19. The operator was advised that he should shut the lease down to cease the discharge. Violations are noted.

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8155917
Permit API: 125-24633
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/09/2023
Comments: On 8/9/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Varner Unit Well Pad in Donegal Township, Washington County in response to a spill reported by the Operator on 8/8/2023 (CTS: 374112Background:On 8/8/2023, a produced water spill of approximately 15 gallons occurred at the Varner Unit Well Pad. The release originated from a pin hole leak from a line inside the 8H GPU Unit. A valve on the line was inadvertently missing an o-ring, causing the leak. Remediation of the spill began on that day with removing the saturation from the gravel surrounding the GPU unit. Remediation resumed the following day with excavation of the impacted gravel. SPSI was on site during the site visit completing the clean up.During the inspection, the following was observed: -The compromised valve and line where the leak began were removed from the 8H GPU unit and were to be replaced (Photo 1).-The extent of the release appeared to have been delineated with on the surface gravel around the GPU Unit (Photos 2-4).- SPSI was on site during the site visit completing the remediation (Photos 5-6).-Conductivity readings were taken within the delineated spill area, 1.2 mS/cm -1.8 mS/cm (Photos 7-9).-Act 9 sign was present at site entrance (Photo 10).Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) were noted and immediately corrected.
